cases.title: concurrent inserts with NEWER keys
notes: New rows sort above every cursor (newer than all frozen rows), so an in-flight traversal never returns them. Frozen set must appear exactly once.

cases.title: concurrent inserts with OLDER keys
notes: New rows sort after every frozen row, so they appear on tail pages as post-watermark extras. Frozen set must appear exactly once; extras are recorded, not counted as miss/dup.

cases.title: concurrent inserts INTERLEAVED in the key range
notes: New rows sort between the two frozen tie groups, so they appear on mid pages. Frozen set must appear exactly once. All four inserts happen before the reader crosses the mid key range (page 9): an insert after page 10 would sort ahead of the page-10 cursor and never be returned — the same cursor-crossing rule L4 documents.

cases.title: concurrent inserts inside a same-timestamp tie group
notes: Tie-group inserts sort between frozen refs. Whether one is returned depends on the cursor at insert time: le-pg-1010a (inserted after page 2, key behind the cursor) is returned; le-pg-1020a / le-pg-1030a (inserted after pages 5/8, keys ahead of the cursor) are never returned. Frozen set must appear exactly once either way.

cases.title: key-changing UPDATE of a NOT-YET-READ row (miss boundary)
notes: le-pg-1030 sits on static page 3. Moving its occurred_at newer than the page-1 cursor moves it ahead of the reader, so it is never returned: exactly that row is MISSED. This is the mechanism boundary: keyset pagination cannot guarantee exactly-once if a sort key changes mid-traversal. Production guards make this write unreachable.

cases.title: key-changing UPDATE of an ALREADY-READ row (duplicate boundary)
notes: le-pg-1040 is read on page 1. Moving its occurred_at older than the page-1 cursor moves it behind the reader, so it is returned AGAIN on the tail page: exactly that row is DUPLICATED. Same boundary as L5. Production guards make this write unreachable.

cases.title: DELETE of a NOT-YET-READ row (absent boundary)
notes: le-pg-1020 sits on static page 5. Deleting it after page 1 means it is never returned: it is ABSENT (recorded as missed-by-deletion, not as a pagination miss). Every other frozen row must appear exactly once. Production guards make this write unreachable; no FK references the ledger table, so nothing else blocks the delete in the experiment schema.

cases.title: control: traversal with NO concurrent writes
notes: Reproduces the stage-7 class-2 traversal on the new baseline: 60 rows, page size 5, 12 pages, frozen set exactly once.

cases.title: MIXED workload: newer + older + tie inserts + delete
notes: Combined stress: the newer insert is never returned; the older, tie and mid inserts are returned as extras (in key order); the deleted row is absent; every other frozen row appears exactly once.
